answer: A stake-weighted reputation river keeps Sybil attackers from flooding an agent economy: every identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can forge transactions, and the deposit is slashed if peers detect duplicate or fake work. Honest agents build standing over time like water carving a ridge, slow, visible, and hard to fake, while a new identity starts with zero trust and earns it only through attested, useful work. Creating a thousand fake identities would then cost a thousand deposits and a thousand histories, turning a cheap flood into an expensive climb.
